title: Birth of the Buddha
description: Siddhartha Gautama is born in the garden of Lumbini according to tradition; the date is disputed and may be a century later.

title: Ashoka's pillar at Lumbini
description: The emperor Ashoka visits the Buddha's birthplace and sets up an inscribed pillar, the oldest dated monument in Nepal.

title: Changu Narayan inscription
description: King Manadeva records his victories on a pillar, the earliest dated inscription of the Kathmandu Valley.

title: Nepal Sambat era begins
description: A new calendar era is started in the Kathmandu Valley and remains in use for a thousand years.

title: Malla dynasty begins
description: Ari Malla becomes the first Malla king of the Kathmandu Valley, whose dynasty rules it for more than five centuries.

title: Death of Yaksha Malla
description: After the king's death the valley is divided among his heirs into the rival kingdoms of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur.

title: Gorkha kingdom founded
description: Dravya Shah seizes the hill town of Gorkha and founds the Shah dynasty that later unifies Nepal.

title: Gorkha conquest of Kathmandu
description: Prithvi Narayan Shah takes Kathmandu during the Indra Jatra festival and makes it the capital of a unified Nepal.

title: Fall of Bhaktapur
description: The last Malla city falls to the Gorkhas, completing the conquest of the Kathmandu Valley.

title: Treaty of Betrawati
description: A Qing army that had crossed the Himalayas after Nepal's invasion of Tibet makes peace near Nuwakot, and Nepal agrees to send tribute to Beijing.

title: Treaty of Sugauli
description: The treaty ending the Anglo-Nepalese War is ratified, and Nepal gives up about a third of its territory and accepts a British resident.

title: Kot massacre
description: Jung Bahadur and his brothers kill dozens of rival nobles in the palace armoury, beginning a century of rule by hereditary Rana prime ministers.

title: Muluki Ain
description: Jung Bahadur Rana issues Nepal's first national legal code, which fixes the caste order in law.

title: Nepal–Britain Treaty
description: Britain formally recognises Nepal as an independent and sovereign state.

title: Nepal–Bihar earthquake
place: Eastern Nepal (epicentre south of Mount Everest)
description: An earthquake of about magnitude 8 kills more than 10,000 people in Nepal and Bihar and destroys much of the Kathmandu Valley's towns.

title: End of Rana rule
description: King Tribhuvan returns from India and proclaims a government including the Nepali Congress, ending 104 years of Rana rule.

title: First ascent of Mount Everest
description: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reach the highest summit on Earth from the Nepalese side.

title: King Mahendra's coup
description: The king dismisses the first elected government, jails prime minister B. P. Koirala and replaces parties with the Panchayat system.

title: People's Movement
description: After weeks of protest King Birendra lifts the ban on political parties and accepts a constitutional monarchy.

title: Maoist insurgency begins
description: The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) attacks police posts in the western hills, starting a ten-year civil war that kills about 17,000 people.

title: Royal massacre
description: King Birendra and eight other members of the royal family are shot dead at a family dinner, according to the official inquiry by Crown Prince Dipendra.

title: King Gyanendra takes direct power
description: The king dismisses the government and declares a state of emergency, uniting the parties and the Maoists against him.

title: Parliament reinstated
description: Nineteen days of mass protest force King Gyanendra to restore the parliament he had dissolved.

title: Comprehensive Peace Accord
description: The government and the Maoists sign an agreement ending the civil war.

title: Monarchy abolished
description: The newly elected Constituent Assembly declares Nepal a federal democratic republic, ending 240 years of Shah kings.

title: Gorkha earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 7.8 kills nearly 9,000 people and damages many of the historic buildings of the Kathmandu Valley.

title: Constitution of 2015
description: A constitution written by the elected assembly comes into force and divides Nepal into seven federal provinces.
